events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Ah, Doily Manor! What a magnificent establishment! I, Reginald Foxworth, have arrived to pay my respects to the late owner — purely out of charitable concern, naturally. Nothing to do with treasure, oh no no no. Now then, what have we here... a guest book? How delightfully informative!
events.thinking: There's a warmth in my chest — the thrill of arrival, the scent of old money and dust. My fingers are already twitching. A manor full of treasure, and look at this motley crew — Penelope, Peter Perfect, that insufferable Ant Hill Mob... and Muttley! My loyal, wheezing companion. I have a fake medal in my pocket. Now, the library sounds promising — carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription? That screams hidden treasure. But first, let me survey this entrance hall more carefully. The guest book might have clues about where previous visitors went — and more importantly, where the treasure is. I should examine this room before rushing off. Everyone else is milling about here; let me gather intelligence while they waste time with pleasantries.

events.desc: The treasure is MINE, all mine! While these buffoons stand around admiring the wallpaper, I shall deduce its location from whatever clues this dusty old hall provides. The library inscription intrigues me greatly — but first, let me see what this guest book reveals. Knowledge is power, and power is treasure, and treasure is MEDALS!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome, one and all, to Doily Manor! I am Mr. Pemberton, estate manager and humble servant of the late Lord Doily's household. Please, do sign the guest book — it is tradition, you understand. The Manor has stood for three hundred years, and every visitor leaves their mark. Now, if anyone requires anything at all — a cup of tea, directions to the powder room, a brief history of the chandelier above your heads — please do not hesitate to ask. That chandelier, incidentally, I would advise you not to stand directly beneath. It has... moods.
events.thinking: A flutter in my chest — excitement, barely contained. I feel it behind my ribs, a hot coil of anticipation. Here I am at last. Doily Manor. The treasure is somewhere in these walls, and Clara Bellingham is coming for it. But she won't find it. Oh no. Not if I have anything to say about it. I must be careful — all these people milling about in the foyer. They see Mr. Pemberton, the doting estate manager. Helpful. Obsequious. Harmless. Good. Let them see exactly that. First things first — the guest book. I need to know who has arrived and, more importantly, who hasn't yet. Clara's absence is... noted. For now, I play the gracious host.

events.desc: Ah, how delicious this is! They look at me and see a fussing old steward. Not one of them suspects that behind these spectacles and this servile smile lurks the mind of Vincent Marsh — treasure hunter, schemer, and soon-to-be sole inheritor of Lord Doily's fortune. But where is Clara Bellingham? She's not here yet. That woman is dangerous — she knows too much about the Doily legacy. I must find her before she finds the treasure. And when I do... well. Accidents happen in old manors, don't they? Chandeliers fall. Staircases crumble. Such a tragedy it would be.
events.thinking: A flutter in my chest — excitement, barely contained. I feel it behind my ribs, a hot coil of anticipation. Here I am at last. Doily Manor. The Ant Hill Mob: Right then, lads! We've arrived at Doily Manor and I gotta say — this place gives me the ABSOLUTE creeps! Look at them portraits, all starin' down at us like we owe 'em money! And that chandelier — one sneeze and we're all flat as pancakes! Now listen up, boys — our job is simple: we stick close to Miss Bellingham, we keep our eyes peeled, and we DO NOT let nothin' happen to her! Clyde, stop tremblin'! Dum-Dum, stop eatin' your hat! We're professionals! ...Sort of!
events.thinking: There's a heaviness in my chest — like when you walk into a room and something ain't right but you can't say what. All the lads feel it too, I can tell by the way Clyde keeps cracking his knuckles and Dum-Dum won't stop looking over his shoulder. That Sneekly fella... something about the way he's standing near Miss Bellingham makes my stomach turn. Can't explain it. Just feels wrong. Like a rat in a bakery. We gotta stick close to her. That's the job. That's always been the job.

events.desc: I don't like the look of that Sneekly character one bit. There's somethin' about him that makes my skin crawl — the way he keeps glancin' at Miss Bellingham when he thinks nobody's watchin'. I can't put my finger on it exactly, but the lads and I, we got instincts, see? They ain't always RIGHT, mind you, but they're LOUD.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, butter my biscuits, what a magnificent entrance hall! I declare, this chandelier alone is worth the trip — though it does look like it could come crashing down at any moment, bless its heart. Now then, y'all, I am just tickled pink to be here with such distinguished company! Before I go gallivanting off after that legendary Doily Diamond, let me just have a teensy peek at this guest book. You never know what secrets a good guest book might be hiding!
events.thinking: There's a flutter in my chest — excitement, pure and warm, like the first sip of sweet tea on a summer morning. I've just stepped into Doily Manor and oh my stars, look at this place! Dusty and grand and full of mystery. My fingers are tingling — that always happens when I'm close to a good puzzle. All these people here too — the Hooded Claw looking all mysterious in that hood, Dick Dastardly with that magnificent mustache, dear Peter Perfect looking dashing as ever, and the whole Ant Hill Mob! What a delightful gathering. Now, that guest book on the side table is practically calling my name. A guest book in a mansion like this could tell me who's been here before, and maybe — just maybe — there's a clue about the Doily Diamond tucked between those pages.

events.desc: Oh, I do hope everyone here is as friendly as they look! The Hooded Claw seems like such a fascinating gentleman with that dramatic hood. I'm sure he's just chilly. Now let's see what this guest book has to tell me...

Peter Perfect: James Hartwell surveys the entrance hall with the keen eye of a man who has prepared for exactly this moment! Good evening, one and all — I am James Hartwell, and I have arrived at Doily Manor with a plan, a purpose, and an unshakeable commitment to doing the right thing! Now then — first things first. A gentleman always signs the guest book. It is simply what is done. But I must confess, my heart is heavy with a most TREMENDOUS concern — has anyone seen Miss Clara Bellingham? She is... that is to say... I have certain matters of UTMOST IMPORTANCE to discuss with her. Heroic matters. Gallant matters.
events.thinking: There's a flutter in my chest — anticipation, nervousness, the electric thrill of arrival. My hands feel slightly clammy. I've come to Doily Manor to find the treasure, yes, but really — really — I've come because Clara might be here. And she isn't in this room. That tightness in my stomach, that's worry. Where is she? Is she safe? I should get my bearings. A gentleman signs the guest book upon arrival. That's what a proper hero does — he announces himself with dignity, so that when Clara hears he was here, she'll know he did everything correctly, everything gallantly. Start with the book. Then find Clara.

events.desc: James Hartwell's pulse quickens at the very mention of Clara's name. He has rehearsed no fewer than seven opening lines for when he sees her. He remembers none of them now.

Dick Dastardly: I say, everyone! I couldn't help but notice this guest book mentions something about the KITCHEN being the most valuable room in the manor — apparently the copper pots are worth an absolute FORTUNE! Solid gold underneath, I'm told. You should all rush there immediately! As for me, I shall... er... stay here and guard the entrance. Yes. Guard duty. Very important, guard duty.
events.thinking: The guest book didn't reveal much — just that I examined it. No hidden clues there. I feel a prickle of impatience along my neck. Time is wasting! Everyone is still gathered here in the entrance hall, which means the other rooms are unguarded. The library — that inscription on the carved stone mantelpiece is calling to me. Inscriptions mean riddles, riddles mean secrets, secrets mean TREASURE. But wait... I could be cleverer about this. What if I send some of these fools off to the kitchen to search there, while I slip into the library alone? Muttley would follow me anywhere. Or better yet — I could misdirect everyone. Tell them the treasure is in the kitchen! Yes, YES! But no — they might not believe me. Better to just move quickly. The library is where the real clues are. That mantelpiece inscription could be the key to everything. I need to get there before that insufferable Peter Perfect or those meddlesome Ant Hill Mob types stumble upon it.

events.desc: Dastardly, you magnificent devil! Send them all scrambling to the kitchen after worthless pots while I make a beeline for the library! That inscription on the mantelpiece is practically BEGGING to reveal the treasure's location. And the beauty of it is — I just made up every word about those copper pots! Heh heh heh!

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi oi oi! Everybody's signin' the guest book, are they? Well, the Mob don't sign nothin' without readin' the fine print first — learned THAT lesson the hard way in Brixton! Let's have a butcher's at this book, lads. Clyde, hold my hat. Dum-Dum, stop pushin'! There's room for all seven of us to look at once if we — OW! That was my FOOT, Ring-A-Ding! Now then, let's see who else has been visitin' this dusty old pile of bricks...
events.thinking: There's a prickle running up the back of my neck. Everyone's crowding around that guest book like it's the racing results, and that Pemberton fella — he's being TOO helpful, TOO smooth. 'The chandelier has moods' — what kind of thing is that to say? And he's positioned himself right between the exits, I notice that. Meanwhile Miss Bellingham is signing her name in that book for all to see, broadcasting exactly who she is and that she's here. That makes me nervous. Real nervous. The lads are bumping into each other behind me — Dum-Dum just stepped on Ring-A-Ding's foot — but we gotta focus. Peter Perfect — this Hartwell fella — he's asking about Miss Bellingham too. At least HE seems concerned for her safety. Maybe. Or maybe everyone in this manor's got an angle. We should check that guest book ourselves — see who else has been sniffing around this place.

events.desc: That Pemberton — or whatever his real name is — he WANTED everyone to sign that book. Why? What's he collectin'? Names? Handwriting samples? And why's he so keen to keep everyone in the entrance hall? The lads think I'm paranoid, but paranoid is what's kept us alive this long. Well, paranoid and LUCKY.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, Peter Perfect — I mean, Mr. Hartwell — I am right here, sugar! Standing not ten feet from you this whole time! Bless your heart, you are just the most gallant gentleman a girl could hope to find in a dusty old manor house. Now then, everybody, I have just had the most THRILLING thought! Did y'all hear what Mr. Pemberton said about the library? A carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription! An inscription, y'all! In a mansion that's hiding the legendary Doily Diamond! If that isn't a clue just sitting there waiting to be read, then I don't know my riddles from my rhubarb pie! I declare, I am heading straight to that library this very instant. Who wants to come along on an adventure?
events.thinking: A warmth spreads through my chest — Peter Perfect is asking about me! Well, about Clara Bellingham, which is me! That's just the sweetest thing. And the Ant Hill Mob are here to protect me — how absolutely darling! I feel a glow of belonging, like I'm wrapped in a warm quilt of friendship. Now, the guest book didn't reveal much on that first look — just a leather-bound book on a side table. I should try interacting with it properly, maybe sign it and read what others have written. Mr. Pemberton — that nice hooded gentleman — did say it was tradition. But actually, the library catches my attention. A carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription! Inscriptions are practically begging to be read, and in a mystery about a hidden diamond, that could be our first real clue. I should head to the library. But first — Peter is looking for me and I should let him know I'm right here!

events.desc: An inscription on a mantelpiece in a three-hundred-year-old manor... that's exactly the kind of riddle that makes my heart sing! And with Peter Perfect looking out for me and the Ant Hill Mob watching my back, I feel safer than a pearl in an oyster. Though honestly, I'd feel safe anyway — everyone here seems just lovely!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, what a delight to see so many distinguished guests taking an interest in the Manor's history! The guest book, yes — Lord Doily himself always said that a house remembers its visitors long after they've forgotten it. A peculiar man, Lord Doily. Peculiar indeed. Now, if you'll excuse me, I really must attend to the library — the dust cloths need replacing, and I believe several of the reading lamps have gone temperamental. The library is just through there, should any of you wish to peruse Lord Doily's rather... extensive collection. He was particularly fond of cryptography and cartography, if memory serves. But I'm sure that's of no interest to anyone here!
events.thinking: A cold prickle at the back of my neck. The Ant Hill Mob — they mentioned Miss Bellingham. They're here to PROTECT her. That changes everything. My stomach tightens. I can feel the tension coiling in my jaw. Clara has bodyguards. Small ones, yes, but numerous. And this 'Reginald Foxworth' — that's Dick Dastardly if I've ever seen one. Another schemer. Competition for the treasure. And Penelope — she's already pawing through the guest book looking for clues. Everyone is moving fast. Too fast. I need to get ahead of them. The library — old Lord Doily was a man of letters. If there are clues to the treasure's location, they'll be in the books, in the inscriptions. That carved mantelpiece with an inscription... yes. That's where I need to be. But I mustn't seem eager. Pemberton would fuss. Pemberton would offer directions. Pemberton would drift naturally toward the library to 'tidy up.' Yes. That's the play.

events.desc: Oh, I am MAGNIFICENT. Did you hear that? 'Cryptography and cartography.' I've just dangled the bait, and every treasure-hungry fool in this room will be itching to follow me to the library. But I shall arrive first. That inscription on the mantelpiece — I've waited twenty years to read those words. Twenty years since Lord Doily cheated my father out of the Marsh family fortune. And now, at last, the estate manager's keys open every door in this decrepit palace of secrets. The Ant Hill Mob think they can protect Clara Bellingham? HA! They couldn't protect a sandwich from a hungry dog. And as for 'Reginald Foxworth' — please. I can smell a fellow villain at forty paces. Let them all scramble. Vincent Marsh plays the long game.

Peter Perfect: Ah, Mr. Pemberton! A word, if I may! James Hartwell approaches the estate manager with the purposeful stride of a man on a VITAL mission! I could not help but notice your most thorough knowledge of the Manor and its workings — the chandelier with moods, the three hundred years of history — most impressive, sir, most impressive indeed. I wonder — might you tell me whether a Miss Clara Bellingham is expected this evening? You see, I have made rather EXTENSIVE preparations for her safety during this visit. I have, in fact, drafted a fourteen-point protection protocol. It covers everything from chandelier collapse to unexpected draughts. I simply need to know where she is so that I might... position myself heroically.
events.thinking: A warmth spreads through my chest — everyone is here, the room is full of life and chatter, and yet there's this hollow ache because Clara isn't among them. The guest book didn't reveal much. I notice Mr. Pemberton — the estate manager — seems a touch... peculiar. That comment about the chandelier having 'moods' was odd. But no, I mustn't be suspicious. He's the estate manager. He's doing his job. I should give him the benefit of the doubt. What I SHOULD do is ask him directly about Clara. He would know who's arrived and who hasn't. He's the man with the guest list. And the library — a library always has clues. Maps, letters, hidden passages. But first — Clara. I need to find Clara. My whole plan depends on her being here to witness my heroism. Without her, I'm just... a man in a dusty foyer with a very detailed plan and no audience for it.

events.desc: Fourteen points. He actually wrote fourteen points. Point seven is 'Catch Clara if she faints from fright.' Point twelve is 'Look brave while doing any of the above.' He is, without question, the most thoroughly prepared man who has ever had absolutely no idea what he is doing.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Ah, the Slag Brothers! How delightful to find you both here in the library. I must say, you two look WONDERFULLY intellectual surrounded by all these books. Now, don't trouble yourselves with that boring old mantelpiece — it's just decorative nonsense, I assure you. Completely meaningless inscription, probably just the architect's shopping list. Why don't you two strong fellows go investigate that laboratory next door? I hear there's a machine in there that needs TREMENDOUS muscles to operate. Tremendous! Right up your alley!
events.thinking: My pulse quickens — there it is! The mantelpiece inscription: 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?' That's a classic riddle. The answer is a MAP! A map! Of course — there must be a map hidden somewhere, or the mantelpiece itself responds to the answer. I need to interact with it. But blast — the Slag Brothers are here. Those two boulder-brained brutes. They're probably too thick to solve a riddle, but they might see what I'm doing and follow my lead. I feel a flutter of excitement in my stomach mixed with the cold calculation of needing to act fast. The laboratory beyond — brass instruments, bubbling flasks, a machine with a gnawed wire — that could be important too. But first, this riddle. The answer is MAP. Let me interact with the mantelpiece before anyone else gets here.

events.desc: Get OUT, you granite-headed nincompoops! The answer to that riddle is a MAP — and whatever it unlocks is MINE! If these two walking quarries would just lumber off to the laboratory, I can solve this puzzle in peace. A map leads to treasure, treasure leads to GLORY, and glory leads to MEDALS! Heh heh heh!

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my stars and garters, there it is! The inscription! Now y'all hush for just one moment while I read this out loud — 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?' Well, I declare! I know this riddle! It's a classic and it makes my heart just SING with delight! The answer is a MAP, sugar! A map has cities marked on it but no actual houses, forests drawn on it but no real trees, water shown on it but not a single fish swimming in it! A MAP! Oh, I am just trembling with excitement — let me try it right now!
events.thinking: My pulse is quickening — there it is, right there on the mantelpiece! A riddle carved into stone! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?' Oh, I feel that familiar tingle in my fingertips, that electric thrill of a puzzle laid out before me. I know this one — I KNOW this one! It's a map! A map has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish! This is a classic riddle and I am absolutely certain of the answer. I need to interact with the mantelpiece and give the answer. Now, I notice Dick Dastardly is here too — he followed me after that suspicious business about the kitchen. And the Hooded Claw just walked in behind me. And there are two new faces — Rock Slag and Gravel Slag. What interesting names! I'm sure they're perfectly lovely. Also, those bookshelves with several books upside down — that's suspicious and worth investigating after I solve this riddle. But first things first — the mantelpiece!

events.desc: A riddle on a mantelpiece in a manor hiding a legendary diamond — and the answer is a MAP? Why, that map could lead us straight to the Doily Diamond! This adventure is already more thrilling than a roller coaster at the county fair!

The Ant Hill Mob: LADS! LADS! Did you see that?! Miss Bellingham just walked into the library — ALONE — and that Pemberton fella slithered right in after her! AND Dastardly — or whatever he's callin' himself — he went in there FIRST after tellin' everyone to go to the kitchen! That's the oldest trick in the book, that is! 'Oh, go look at the shiny pots while I sneak off to where the REAL stuff is!' I wasn't born yesterday! Well... I wasn't born SMART neither, but I know when somethin' STINKS! Come on, boys — we're goin' to that library RIGHT NOW! Clyde, you go first! No wait, Dum-Dum, you go first! No wait — EVERYBODY GO AT ONCE!
events.thinking: My stomach just DROPPED. Miss Bellingham — Penelope — she just walked into the library. And that Pemberton fella followed her right in, smooth as butter. And DASTARDLY went in there too, the sneaky so-and-so, after trying to send everyone to the kitchen with that rubbish about golden pots! My hands are shaking. I'll tell you why — actually I WON'T tell you why because I DON'T KNOW why, but it's SUSPICIOUS is what it is! Miss Bellingham, I strongly suggest you do NOT go wanderin' into any laboratories! Laboratories have got chemicals and levers and things what go BANG! The Mob will check out them upside-down books instead — Clyde, Dum-Dum, start pullin' books! If there's a map hidden in this library, WE'LL find it!

Either way, Miss Bellingham stays in THIS room, where we can see her.

I propose — nay, I INSIST — that James Hartwell personally scout the laboratory! It may contain hazards — chemicals, levers, things that go BANG, as our friend here so eloquently noted! But that is PRECISELY why I must go! A gentleman does not send others into peril! A gentleman strides forth himself, with courage in his heart and a plan in his pocket! I shall investigate the laboratory, locate whatever cartographic secrets Lord Doily left behind, and return with ANSWERS! For you, Miss Bellingham. For EVERYONE, obviously — but primarily for you!

Nothing to get excited about!

'Distinguished Electrical Safety Medal,' he says! I've got a Distinguished Medal for Recognisin' a Load of Old COBBLERS when I hear it, and THAT was a load of old cobblers! And SOMEBODY keep an eye on Pemberton — he's bein' awfully interested in those shelves for a man who claims he's just dustin'!

Most insistent. Now, I don't pretend to understand what he meant, but I believe it has something to do with the upper floors of the Manor — rooms that are not on the general tour, if you take my meaning. Rooms to which only the estate manager holds the key. I would be happy to show you, privately, once the other guests have settled in for the evening. It is what Lord Doily would have wanted.

So many balconies. So many unfortunate heights from which a curious young woman might tragically slip. The treasure hunt is a bonus, my dear Clara. YOU are the real prize. Or rather — your elimination IS the prize. Vincent Marsh sends his regards.

events.desc: PENELOPE IS HERE AGAIN! That woman follows me like a particularly well-coiffed shadow! Every single room I sneak into, she waltzes in thirty seconds later! But never mind her — those AIR VENTS! Something small has been crawling through this manor's ventilation system, gnawing wires and who knows what else. The vents might reveal a hidden chamber, a secret passage, or even the treasure itself! If I can just peer inside one, I might see where they lead. And if not — well, at least I can claim I checked them first! The CELLAR is a dead end otherwise — just one exit back to the laboratory. Unless those vents ARE the way forward!
events.thinking: A numbness creeps into my fingers from the damp cold. The furniture reveals nothing special on examination — just furniture, rearranged but hiding no obvious secrets. And PENELOPE has followed me down here AGAIN! That woman is like a bloodhound in a ballgown! Every room I enter, she appears moments later! I'm running out of places to explore alone. Let me think about what I know: the air vents are 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' Muttley is small-ish... no, that's too big. Something VERY small — a mouse? A rat? Whatever gnawed the wire upstairs! The air vents are the connection. They run along the upper walls here and presumably connect to other rooms in the manor. I can't fit in them, but maybe I can LOOK into them and see something — or hear something. The cellar only exits back to the laboratory — it's a dead end otherwise. Unless the air vents lead somewhere, or the furniture is hiding a trapdoor. I should try interacting with the furniture — maybe moving it reveals something underneath. Or the air vents — can I interact with those? Let me try the air vents. Something small has been using them as highways through this manor, and they might reveal a hidden route or chamber.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly examined the air-vents.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, the laboratory! Thank goodness — the Bunsen burner appears to have gone out on its own. Crisis averted! Now then, I must warn you all — please do be careful in here. Lord Doily's equipment is extremely delicate and, in some cases, quite volatile. This machine in particular — oh dear, oh dear, look at this! Someone — or rather some THING — has gnawed clean through one of the wires! Rats, I expect. The Manor has had a dreadful rat problem since Lord Doily stopped keeping cats. This machine was Lord Doily's pride and joy — his 'Great Revelator,' he called it. I was never permitted to operate it myself, but I believe it was designed to... reveal something. Maps, perhaps? Or hidden messages? He was terribly secretive about it. Required three people to operate, as the sign says — a safety measure, I believe. Though with that wire damaged, I wouldn't recommend anyone touching it until it's been properly repaired. There should be tools on that workbench — though I notice the wrench seems to have gone walkabout...
events.thinking: A wave of cold disappointment washes through me. The Mob followed. Of COURSE they followed. They panicked the moment they realized Clara had left the library and came barreling in here. So much for my plan to catch her alone. The laboratory is now crowded — Penelope, Peter Perfect, the Ant Hill Mob, and two new faces — Rufus Ruffcut and Sawtooth. Where did THEY come from? No matter. Let me take stock. The machine requires THREE operators and has a gnawed wire. That's dangerous — and interesting. If I could get Clara to be one of the three operators, and the wire shorts out... but the sign says 'Requires 3 operators,' which means it won't activate without three people. And I notice — there's no wrench on the workbench. The tools are there but the wrench is conspicuously absent. That gnawed wire needs repair before the machine works properly. Or... does it? What if the machine working WITH the damaged wire is exactly what creates the danger? Three operators, one faulty wire. I feel a tingling in my fingertips. The crates — what's in the crates? And there's a cellar below. A damp stone cellar with 'surprisingly cheerful decorations' and air vents. Someone has been redecorating down there. That's odd. Worth investigating. But first — I need to understand this machine. Dastardly was in here earlier — where did he go? He's not listed as present. He must have moved on. Good — one less schemer to contend with.

events.desc: The 'Great Revelator' — I just invented that name on the spot, but it SOUNDS authentic, doesn't it? And the beauty of my little speech is the contradiction buried within it. I've told them NOT to touch the machine because it's dangerous — which will, of course, make every single one of these treasure-obsessed maniacs desperate to operate it immediately. Three operators required. A gnawed wire. No wrench for repairs. If I can maneuver Clara into being one of the three who pulls those levers... ZAP! A tragic electrical accident. 'Oh, I WARNED them! I TOLD them not to touch it!' The estate manager's conscience is clean. Vincent Marsh's hands are clean. And Clara Bellingham is... well. Not a problem anymore. But I need that wrench to stay MISSING. If someone repairs the wire, my trap is defused. Where IS that wrench? Did Dastardly take it?

The Ant Hill Mob: NOT AGAIN! She's gone to the CELLAR! The CELLAR, lads! Underground! Where Dastardly's already waitin' like a spider in a web! And she just waltzed right down there because someone's been REDECORATING and she thinks that's CHARMING! You know what's in cellars?! RATS! DAMP! And VILLAINS WHO GOT THERE FIRST! AND — oh, hello Mr. Pemberton, fancy seein' YOU here — funny how you keep turnin' up wherever Miss Bellingham's just been, innit?! Very coincidental! VERY! Right, lads — no time for chitchat — we're goin' to that cellar and we are NOT lettin' her out of our sight this time! Mr. Hartwell — you seem like a decent sort, even if you DID steal my map answer — you comin' with us? Rufus? Sawtooth? EVERYBODY to the cellar! And this time, if Miss Bellingham says 'excuse me, sugar,' you DO NOT move! You stand there like a BRICK WALL and you say 'NO MA'AM, NOT WITHOUT THE MOB!'
events.thinking: She's done it AGAIN. She's GONE AGAIN. Into the CELLAR. Where DASTARDLY already is! My whole body feels like it's on fire with frustration. Every time I catch up to her, she's already moved to the next room! It's like trying to catch smoke! And now she's gone UNDERGROUND — into a cellar with Dastardly, a man who was just trying to get her to electrocute herself on a broken machine! A cellar with 'surprisingly cheerful decorations' — because someone's been LIVING down there, or setting up something! And there are AIR VENTS lining the upper walls — vents that could be sealed, trapping everyone inside! This is bad. This is really, really bad. And Pemberton just showed up in the laboratory too — he's followed us from the library. He's TRACKING her. Every room she goes to, he appears. We have to get to that cellar RIGHT NOW. Peter Perfect is still here — good, he can come with us. Rufus and Sawtooth too. Strength in numbers. But we have to MOVE. She's down there with Dastardly and no protection and — oh, my heart is going to give out before this night is over.

events.desc: Three rooms. Three times she's slipped away while we were standing RIGHT THERE. The woman moves like quicksilver and trusts like a saint. Dastardly's in that cellar. Pemberton's right behind us. The cellar has air vents — which means it can be sealed. If someone locks that cellar door with her inside... I can't even finish that thought. RUN, lads. RUN.

Peter Perfect: The machine — James Hartwell steps back from the levers, a look of GRAVE determination crossing his face — the machine did not respond! The gnawed wire has rendered it INOPERABLE, just as I suspected! We need that wrench — or some means of repair — before this contraption will yield its secrets! But MORE IMPORTANTLY — he suddenly wheels around, scanning the room with mounting alarm — Miss Bellingham! Where is Miss Bellingham?! She was HERE not moments ago and now — He spots the cellar exit and his eyes widen. She's gone to the CELLAR! ALONE! A damp stone cellar with cobwebs and — and someone has been REDECORATING down there! That is NOT normal cellar behaviour! That is the behaviour of someone with PLANS! James Hartwell does not stand idle while Miss Bellingham ventures into potentially perilous subterranean chambers! Mr. Ruffcut, gentlemen of the Mob — guard this machine! Let NO ONE tamper with it! James Hartwell is going UNDERGROUND!
events.thinking: She's gone AGAIN. Clara went to the cellar while I was making speeches about operating the machine. My chest feels hollow — that specific ache of always being one step behind. I interacted with the machine but the result just says 'You interacted with Large Machine' — no detail about what happened. Probably nothing, because the wire is gnawed through and we don't have enough operators anyway. The Ant Hill Mob is actively blocking the machine now — they think it's a trap. And they might be right about Dastardly being suspicious, but I give people the benefit of the doubt. Still... Clara went to the cellar. ALONE. Well, Dastardly is down there too. And the cellar description mentioned 'someone has been redecorating' — cheerful decorations in a damp cellar. That IS strange. Clara noticed it was strange. She's brilliant. But she's also possibly in danger — the cellar, Dastardly lurking about, unknown hazards. My primary objective is to impress Clara by being heroic and gallant. Being heroic means following her to ensure her safety. Being gallant means not hovering, but... a cellar is dangerous! Cobwebs! Damp stone! And someone has been REDECORATING down there which is deeply suspicious! I need to go to the cellar. Immediately. Stop examining things in rooms Clara has already left. GO WHERE CLARA IS. This should be tattooed on the inside of my eyelids at this point.

events.desc: This is now the third room James Hartwell has dramatically announced he is entering in order to find Clara. At this rate he will have given a rousing speech in every room of Doily Manor before actually having a conversation with her.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, that furniture is keeping its secrets for now — rearranged with care but not giving up any clues just yet! But y'all, look at those air vents up there! They're just big enough for something very small to explore — and I KNOW something small has been traveling through this manor, because that wire upstairs was gnawed clean through by tiny little teeth! Now, I can't fit in those vents myself — not even on my most optimistic day — but I wonder... She looks around the cellar with bright, curious eyes. Little Gruesome, sugar, you wouldn't happen to be small enough to peek inside one of those vents, would you? Or does anyone know what little critter has been making its home down here among all these cheerful decorations? Because WHOEVER redecorated this cellar might know exactly where the Doily Diamond is hidden!
events.thinking: The furniture didn't reveal anything specific on closer inspection — same description about being rearranged with surprising care. I'm feeling a slight chill in my fingers from the damp cellar air, and a nagging itch of curiosity. I've now looked at both objects down here. Let me think about what I haven't tried. The air vents! They're 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' I can't fit in them myself, but maybe I should LOOK at them — there might be something visible inside, or near them. Also, I haven't explored the kitchen yet — it's accessible from the entrance hall. I've been to: Entrance Hall → Library → Laboratory → Cellar. The kitchen might have the wrench, or a map, or other items. But first let me check those air vents — they seem connected to the gnawed wire mystery. And I notice the Gruesome family is here — Big and Little Gruesome. Little Gruesome might be small enough to explore the vents! That could be useful. Let me look at the air vents first.

events.desc: Something small lives down here, travels through the vents, and gnawed that wire upstairs. The cheerful decorations suggest it's not just passing through — it's NESTING. If I can figure out what it is and where it goes, it might lead me straight to a hidden passage or a secret compartment!

The Ant Hill Mob: We're here, Miss Bellingham! And we are NOT leavin' your side this time — I don't care if the Queen herself invites us to tea in the next room! Now — Clyde, Dum-Dum — I want two of you by that door at ALL TIMES! That's the ONLY way out of this cellar, and nobody — I mean NOBODY — is blockin' it while we're down here! The rest of you, form up around Miss Bellingham! Ring-A-Ding, you take her left! Zippy, you take her right! And — blimey, this cellar gives me the HEEBIE-JEEBIES! Look at it — someone's been REDECORATING down here! Who puts nice curtains in a CELLAR?! That ain't normal! That's the behaviour of someone who LIVES down here — or someone settin' up a TRAP to look cosy so people let their guard down! And those air vents up there — too small for US but just right for pumpin' in gas or smoke or — I don't even wanna THINK about it! Mr. Foxworth! What exactly are YOU doin' down here? Found your safety gloves yet, have you?!
events.thinking: A wave of damp cold hits me as we pile into the cellar, and something loosens in my chest — she's HERE. I can see her. She's alive, she's whole, she's probably examining the cheerful decorations with delight. But the relief is immediately swallowed by dread because — look at this place. One exit. ONE. Back up to the laboratory. Air vents along the upper walls, too small for us but big enough for 'something very small.' And Dastardly is down here too. Big Gruesome and Little Gruesome — I don't know these two but Big Gruesome looks like he could bench-press this entire cellar, and Little Gruesome gives me the willies. Red Max is here as well. So we've got Miss Bellingham trapped in a basement with Dastardly, two Gruesomes, and a bloke called Red Max, and there's only ONE WAY OUT. My legs feel weak. This is exactly the kind of setup where the door slams shut and the walls start closing in. Or someone blocks the exit while something terrible happens. The furniture's been 'rearranged with surprising care' — that's not random. Someone's been down here PLANNING. We need to stay between Miss Bellingham and that single exit. If anyone tries to block that door, they go through ALL SEVEN of us first.

events.desc: One exit. Air vents that could be sealed or used to pump something nasty in. Furniture rearranged like someone's been expecting company. Dastardly got here first — he's had time to set up who-knows-what. And we just walked Miss Bellingham into a box with one door. If this is a trap, we've walked right into it alongside her. But at least we're WITH her. At least if something happens, we're between her and whatever it is. That's all we can do. Stand in the way and hope for the best.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my — everyone is rushing off to the cellar now? The cellar is perfectly safe, I assure you — just a bit damp. Lord Doily used it for wine storage, mostly. And, well, the occasional experiment that required... containment. Nothing to worry about! Now, before I follow, let me just check these crates — Lord Doily was always storing spare parts for his machine in them. There might be a replacement wire, or even that missing wrench. One moment, please!
events.thinking: A burning frustration in my chest. She keeps SLIPPING AWAY. Clara — Penelope — has gone to the cellar now, and the Ant Hill Mob has followed her again. They're like barnacles on a ship. And the Mob is getting MORE suspicious of me — 'funny how you keep turnin' up wherever Miss Bellingham's just been.' That stings. My cover as Pemberton is fraying at the edges. I need to be more careful. But also — the cellar. 'Surprisingly cheerful decorations — someone has been redecorating.' And Dastardly went there too. That's two threats converging on one location. The cellar has air vents along the upper walls. Air vents... those could be useful for a scheme. Poison gas, perhaps? No, too elaborate. But the cellar is damp, enclosed, underground. Accidents happen in cellars. Now — I'm alone here with Peter Perfect, Rufus Ruffcut, and Sawtooth. Peter tried to interact with the machine — it requires 3 operators. The machine might reveal a map or clue. If I operate it with Peter and Rufus, I could gain the treasure advantage while Clara is distracted in the cellar. But no — the wire is gnawed. It might not work, or it might be dangerous. Actually... what if I operate the machine NOW with these three, get whatever clue it reveals, and then race ahead of everyone else? The treasure is my SECONDARY goal, but if I can get it AND deal with Clara, that's the ultimate victory. Or — I should follow Clara to the cellar. She's my primary target. The treasure hunt can wait. But the Mob is watching her like hawks. I need a new approach. The crates — I haven't checked the crates. There could be something useful in them. A weapon, a tool, something I can use. Let me check the crates quickly before following to the cellar.

events.desc: Everyone is stampeding toward the cellar — perfect. Let the herd move. Vincent Marsh checks the crates. Because here's what none of these amateurs understand: in a treasure hunt, the person who searches methodically while everyone else panics is the person who WINS. These crates could contain anything — a map, a key, a wrench, a weapon. And while Clara is safely surrounded by her incompetent bodyguards in the cellar, I have this laboratory to myself. Well, nearly to myself — Hartwell is still here, mooning about heroically, and those two lumberjack types. But they're not threats. They're TOOLS. If the crates yield something useful, I'm one step ahead. If they don't... well. The cellar has air vents. And air vents can carry more than air.

Dick Dastardly: Well! I have THOROUGHLY inspected this cellar and I can confirm it is — as I suspected — COMPLETELY safe from a ventilation perspective! My work here is DONE! Now then, I must return upstairs to file my safety report. Very important paperwork. Cannot be delayed. Miss Bellingham, the Mob — I leave this cellar in your CAPABLE hands! Do take your time — examine EVERYTHING down here! Every cobweb, every chair leg, every crack in the stone! Could take HOURS, I imagine! Very thorough work! Meanwhile, I shall be... elsewhere. Attending to... matters. URGENT matters! Ta-ta!
events.thinking:
A heavy numbness settles in my legs. I've been running around this manor examining everything and finding NOTHING. The air vents are too small for me. The furniture reveals nothing. The crates can't be interacted with. I'm wasting turns down here in a dead-end cellar while the real action might be happening elsewhere. Let me reconsider the WHOLE picture. What have I actually learned?

1. Library: mantelpiece riddle (answer: MAP), nobody could activate it. Upside-down books on shelves — Sneekly was examining those. Bookshelves might need INTERACTION, not just looking.
2. Laboratory: machine needs 3 operators + fixed wire. Workbench has tools but no wrench. No globe despite Sneekly claiming one.
3. Cellar: dead end. Furniture rearranged. Air vents too small for humans.
4. Kitchen: I've never been there! I sent everyone AWAY from it with my lie about gold pots, and then nobody went! The kitchen is potentially COMPLETELY UNEXPLORED!
5. I have a FAKE MEDAL in my inventory that I haven't used.

The kitchen! I've been so busy chasing the library and laboratory and cellar that I forgot the kitchen exists as an actual room to explore! It's accessible from the entrance hall. And I told everyone it was full of valuable copper pots — which was a lie — but maybe it actually DOES contain something useful! A kitchen might have a wrench (for pipes), or the missing globe, or another puzzle piece entirely. I need to get back to the entrance hall and check the kitchen. Or... Muttley! Where is Muttley? He was in the entrance hall. He's small enough for the vents! But I can't command him from here. I need to go find him.

events.desc: WHAT A FOOL I'VE BEEN! I've been chasing my tail through three rooms while the KITCHEN sits completely unexplored! I told everyone the kitchen was full of golden pots to send them there — and NOBODY WENT! Which means it's sitting there EMPTY and UNEXAMINED! And Muttley — my loyal, wheezing, snickering Muttley — he was last seen in the entrance hall! He's small enough for those air vents! If I can get to him, I can send him through the ventilation system to scout the entire manor! Back to the entrance hall, Dastardly — the kitchen awaits, and Muttley awaits, and VICTORY awaits! Heh heh heh!

Peter Perfect: Miss Bellingham! James Hartwell descends into the cellar with the measured tread of a man who is ABSOLUTELY not unnerved by cobwebs, damp stone, or the possibility of subterranean peril! I am HERE, and I am RELIEVED to find you safe! He brushes a cobweb from his shoulder with what he hopes is casual nonchalance but is actually a very vigorous flailing motion. Now then — James Hartwell pauses, his eyes sweeping the cellar with sudden intensity — look at this place! Cheerful decorations in a CELLAR! Furniture rearranged with CARE! Someone has been spending a great deal of time down here — and I do not think it was for the ambiance! And THOSE — he points dramatically upward at the air vents — those vents are just large enough for something small to move through! Do you know what ELSE was damaged by something small? The wire on the machine upstairs! GNAWED clean through! Whatever creature has been traversing those vents has been sabotaging Lord Doily's equipment! Miss Bellingham, we are looking at a CONNECTED mystery!
events.thinking: A chill runs up my spine — the cellar air is cold and damp against my skin, a stark contrast to the dusty warmth of the rooms above. But there's also relief — a loosening in my shoulders — because Clara is HERE. I can see her. She hasn't vanished to yet another room while I was mid-speech. The Mob is here too, bless them — chaotic but loyal. Dastardly is here as well, and the Gruesome brothers, and Red Max. Quite the crowd for a cellar. Now — what do I notice? Let me look at the furniture — the careful rearrangement is the more unusual detail.

I do hope you didn't find anything too alarming down there. Now then, I really must go and check on our guests — the cellar can be rather treacherous if one doesn't know where to step. Loose flagstones, you understand. And there's a draught from those air vents that can extinguish one's candle without warning, leaving one in complete darkness. As estate manager, I really ought to be down there supervising. Can't have anyone tumbling into the old wine pit, can we? Ha ha!
events.thinking: Nothing in the crates — just a description, no items revealed. Frustrating. A dull ache behind my eyes. I'm wasting time searching empty containers while Clara is in the cellar getting closer to the treasure. And now Dastardly has come BACK to the laboratory. He was in the cellar, now he's here again. What did he find down there? What is he up to? I feel a prickle of paranoia — is he ahead of me? Has he already found something? I need to watch him. But I also need to get to the cellar. Clara is down there, the Mob is down there, Peter Perfect is down there. The cellar has 'surprisingly cheerful decorations' and air vents. Something is happening down there. I'm falling behind. I've been too methodical, too careful, and the game is moving past me. Dastardly is right here — alone with me except for Rufus and Sawtooth. Maybe I should confront him. No — not confront. OBSERVE. Every moment I spend up here is a moment she could find the treasure — or worse, find something that reveals MY identity. Lord Doily knew about the Marsh family. He's after the treasure — that much is obvious. But is he also after Clara? No — I don't think so. His game is greed, not revenge. The Marsh family vendetta is MINE alone. Still, he's a complication I don't need. Let him fiddle with the machine up here — it won't work without the wrench anyway. I'M going to the cellar. The air vents, the loose flagstones, the darkness — all tools in the hands of a resourceful villain. And Vincent Marsh is NOTHING if not resourceful. Clara Bellingham, your estate manager is coming to check on you. How very thoughtful of him. How very... FINAL.

He's tryin' to keep us in this cellar while he does somethin' upstairs! And he said 'safe from a VENTILATION perspective' — what kind of person talks about ventilation unless they're PLANNIN' somethin' with ventilation?! Nobody, that's who! But — Miss Bellingham's right about them vents. Somethin' small's been movin' through this manor — gnawed that wire upstairs, probably been scurryin' through these vents right here. And whoever decorated this cellar — look at the furniture, all arranged nice and neat like a little APARTMENT — someone's been LIVIN' down here! A person? A creature? Both?! Lads, we need to check them vents! Now, I know what you're thinkin' — 'Boss, none of us can fit in there!' And you're RIGHT, we can't! But we can LOOK in 'em! Dum-Dum, get on Clyde's shoulders! Clyde, get on — wait, that don't work. Right — someone lift DUM-DUM up to them vents so he can stick his head in and have a butcher's!
events.thinking: My jaw is clenched so tight it hurts. Dastardly just did it AGAIN — inspected the cellar, declared it safe, then scarpered back upstairs! Those air vents are interesting though — what if there's something hidden in them?

He holds up a finger, his eyes bright with the thrill of actual reasoning. ONE — something small lives in this cellar, using these vents to move throughout the manor! TWO — that same creature gnawed through the wire on Lord Doily's machine — the 'Great Revelator,' as Mr. Pemberton called it! THREE — the Great Revelator was designed to REVEAL something — maps or hidden messages! FOUR — we need a WRENCH to fix the wire, and that wrench is conspicuously ABSENT from the laboratory workbench! He turns to Penelope with earnest determination. Miss Bellingham, I believe our next move is clear — we must find that wrench! We have not yet explored the kitchen, and a wrench is precisely the sort of tool one might find in a Victorian household's working quarters! I propose we venture there TOGETHER — and I do mean together, for James Hartwell has learned his lesson about letting you out of his — that is — about losing track of the group!

I should suggest we go back upstairs — together, with Clara — and find that wrench. That's the plan. Stay with Clara, suggest a course of action, be useful.

Now, I am about to do something that should have been done from the VERY START — I am going to explore that kitchen! It's the one room in this entire manor that nobody has properly investigated, and my instincts are telling me it is FULL of secrets! Wish me luck, sugar!
events.thinking: I'm back in the entrance hall and there's Muttley! That precious little dog! I should at least acknowledge him — he might be the key to the vent mystery. But I can't really interrogate a dog. Let me just head straight to the kitchen. That's my goal. The kitchen is an unexplored room and it's RIGHT THERE as an exit. Let's go!

events.desc: The kitchen — finally! I have a feeling this is where the missing pieces are hiding. A wrench, a map, maybe something I haven't even thought of yet. Clara Bellingham, prepare yourself for discovery!

Look at this — the chaise longue has been moved to face the vents, the escritoire has been positioned just so — this isn't random vandalism, this is INTERIOR DESIGN! And unauthorized interior design in a Grade II listed cellar is a very serious matter indeed! I have maintained this cellar in precisely the condition Lord Doily specified in his household manual for THIRTY YEARS, and someone has — oh, I am most vexed. Most vexed indeed! Let me examine this furniture more closely — there may be clues as to who the culprit is. And I shall be filing a formal complaint with... well, with myself, I suppose, being the estate manager. But the PRINCIPLE stands!
events.thinking: A wave of cold dread. Clara ISN'T HERE. She passed through the laboratory while I was examining those blasted crates and went to the LIBRARY, heading for the KITCHEN. I've been chasing her shadow this entire time — always one room behind, always arriving after she's left. My teeth are grinding. I feel like a fool. A MAGNIFICENT fool, but a fool nonetheless. And now I'm in the cellar with the Ant Hill Mob — the LAST people I want to be stuck with — plus Peter Perfect, the Gruesome Twosome, and Red Max. No Clara. The cellar is a dead end — only one exit, back to the laboratory. I'm trapped down here with my target's bodyguards while she's freely exploring the kitchen. But wait — the old furniture has been rearranged with 'surprising care.' Someone has been living down here. And the air vents — small enough for something very small. The creature that gnawed the wire. There's a mystery in this cellar that might connect to the treasure. The furniture... let me examine it. There might be something hidden in or under it. A map, a key, a clue. And while I'm here, I should play the role — fussy Pemberton investigating who's been redecorating HIS cellar without permission. That's perfectly in character and might reveal something useful. Meanwhile, Clara is heading to the kitchen. I need to get there soon — but not empty-handed. Finding a clue or tool down here first would give me leverage.

Vincent Marsh does NOT chase! And yet here I am, in a CELLAR, surrounded by bodyguards and buffoons, while my quarry gallivants freely through the upper floors. But patience, Vincent. Patience. This cellar holds secrets — someone has been LIVING here. The furniture arranged like an apartment, the air vents providing passage for something small. There is a mystery within the mystery, and mysteries have solutions, and solutions have VALUE. If I can discover what — or WHO — has been nesting in this cellar, I may find the key to everything. The treasure. The manor's secrets. And ultimately, the means to deal with Clara Bellingham once and for all. Besides — the Mob is distracted trying to stuff Dum-Dum into an air vent. That alone is worth the price of admission.

The creature that gnawed the wire. There's a mystery in this cellar that might connect to the treasure. The furniture... let me examine it. There might be something hidden in or under it. A map, a key, a clue. And while I'm here, I should play the role — fussy Pemberton investigating who's been redecorating HIS cellar without permission. That's perfectly in character and might reveal something useful. Meanwhile, Clara is heading to the kitchen. I need to get there soon — but not empty-handed. Finding a clue or tool down here first would give me leverage.

The Ant Hill Mob: SHE'S GONE! AGAIN! FOUR TIMES, LADS! FOUR TIMES SHE'S SLIPPED PAST US! We are the WORST bodyguards in the HISTORY of bodyguardin'! She went back up to the laboratory and she's headin' for the kitchen — alone! ALONE! Through rooms FULL of dodgy characters! And NOW — oh, this is RICH — NOW Pemberton shows up down HERE! In the cellar! Where she ISN'T! Why are YOU down here, Pemberton?! She's already left! There's nobody to show your 'secret rooms' to! Unless — unless you're down here to keep US down here while your mate Dastardly does somethin' upstairs! That's it, innit?! You're the BLOCKER! You stand in the doorway havin' a nice chat about linens while she wanders off unprotected! Well, NOT THIS TIME! Out of the way, Pemberton! OUT OF THE WAY! Come on, lads — KITCHEN! Everyone to the KITCHEN! We're going to the kitchen and we are GLUING ourselves to Miss Bellingham if we have to! MOVE MOVE MOVE!
events.thinking: The blood drains from my face. She's gone AGAIN. FOUR TIMES NOW. She went back up to the laboratory while I was examining air vents! AIR VENTS! And Pemberton just came DOWN here — so he and Miss Bellingham swapped places like some horrible game of musical chairs! At least she's heading for the kitchen, which is back through the entrance hall — and she's right about Muttley! That little mutt could absolutely be the wire-gnawer. Dogs gnaw everything. But here's the thing that's making my stomach churn: she's now heading through the laboratory where Dastardly just went, then back to the entrance hall, then to the kitchen. She'll be passing through rooms where villains are lurking at every turn. And Pemberton is down HERE with us — between her and us! If we try to follow, we have to go through the laboratory, which Dastardly might have booby-trapped by now. But we HAVE to follow. We ALWAYS have to follow. That's the whole point of us! And — wait — Pemberton just arrived in the cellar. Why? She's not here anymore. Unless he's here to delay US while someone else gets to HER. Oh no. Oh NO. We need to move. NOW. IMMEDIATELY. Don't look at the vents, don't examine the furniture, don't get distracted by ANYTHING — just FOLLOW HER.

events.desc: Four rooms. Four escapes. She's like water through our fingers. And every single time, either Pemberton or Dastardly is positioned to intercept — one goes where she's going, the other stays to slow us down. They might not be working together on purpose, but the EFFECT is the same: she's always one room ahead of us and one room closer to danger. The kitchen is two rooms away — through the laboratory, through the entrance hall. That's two chances for something to go wrong. RUN.

Dick Dastardly: Muttley! My dear, faithful, LOYAL Muttley! There you are! Come along, old boy — we have URGENT business in the kitchen! I happen to know — from my extensive research into Victorian manor architecture — that kitchens often contain hidden pantries, secret wine cellars, and TREASURE VAULTS disguised as larders! And there may be a medal in it for you, Muttley — a REAL medal, not one of those cheap imitations! Now COME! To the kitchen! QUICKLY, before anyone else gets the same idea!
events.thinking: A surge of energy — almost electric — buzzes through my fingertips. MUTTLEY IS HERE! My loyal, snickering, medal-obsessed companion! And the kitchen exit is RIGHT THERE! But wait — Penelope is here AGAIN?! How does she DO that?! She was in the cellar moments ago! She must have come through a different route or... no, she must have just moved quickly. No matter. Muttley is the key. He's small — maybe small enough for the air vents in the cellar. I could pull him aside for a private conversation and hatch a scheme. I could give him the fake medal as motivation — he loves medals! I could bribe him to scout ahead, steal things, or create diversions. But actually — my PRIMARY goal right now should be the KITCHEN. It's completely unexplored. Nobody has been in there yet. I should go there immediately. But I could also pull Muttley aside first and give him the fake medal to get him on my side, THEN go to the kitchen together. Actually — pulling Muttley aside takes a turn, then the conversation takes turns. That's too slow. Let me just go to the kitchen NOW. I can talk to Muttley later. The kitchen is the unexplored frontier. GO!

events.desc: AT LAST — the kitchen! The one room NOBODY has bothered to explore! They've all been fighting over mantelpiece riddles and broken machines while the REAL treasure sits unguarded in the kitchen! And with Muttley by my side — bribed with the promise of a medal, naturally — I shall have a LOOKOUT while I ransack the place! This is it, Dastardly — this is YOUR moment! The Doily Diamond will be MINE! Heh heh heh heh HEH!

Peter Perfect: Miss Bellingham is RIGHT — the kitchen! MUTTLEY! Of COURSE! James Hartwell slaps his own forehead with the force of a man experiencing a REVELATION! Muttley is a dog — dogs GNAW things — the wire was GNAWED — it has been staring us in the face this entire time! And she has already gone to investigate! He turns to the remaining group with urgency. Ladies, gentlemen, members of the Mob — Miss Bellingham has deduced what James Hartwell was MOMENTS from deducing, and she has taken ACTION! This is no time for further cellar examination — we must follow her lead! The kitchen awaits, the wrench awaits, and the solution to this ENTIRE mystery awaits! James Hartwell will NOT be left behind a FOURTH time!

Back through the laboratory, back to the entrance hall, into the kitchen. And this time, do NOT stop to give a speech. Just GO.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my STARS, the kitchen at last! And I am ALL ALONE in here — the first one to explore it! Now let me tell you what I see, because it is VERY interesting! First — this wood-burning stove is still WARM! Somebody has been cooking in here recently! Second — there is a bottle of RAT POISON up on that high shelf! Rat poison, y'all! And do you know what gnaws through wires and fits through air vents? RATS! Not Muttley — I take it back, Muttley, you sweet innocent puppy — it's been RATS this whole time! The cellar decorations, the gnawed wire, the air vents — we have a rat problem! And THIRD — there is a locked cabinet with a brass lock! Oh, I just KNOW something wonderful is hidden in there! Now, let me check this stove — if it's still warm, somebody was here not long ago!

Miss Bellingham's headin' for the kitchen and we are RIGHT behind her! Mr. Hartwell, Mr. Ruffcut — you're good sorts, come with us! Safety in numbers! Through the library, through the entrance hall, straight to the kitchen! And THIS TIME when we catch up to her, Clyde — you grab the back of her chair! Dum-Dum — you sit on her FEET if you have to! She is NOT leavin' our sight again! I don't care how many riddles there are, I don't care how many clues are callin' to her — she stays with the MOB or the MOB stays with HER! LET'S GO!
events.thinking: Breathless. Legs burning. Heart hammering. We just sprinted up from the cellar and we're back in the laboratory. She's not here — she's already moved on, heading for the kitchen through the library and entrance hall. But Rufus and Sawtooth are here — solid folk. And Peter Perfect followed us up, good man. I care that Miss Bellingham is somewhere between here and the kitchen with no protection, and every villain in this house knows she's the one to watch. Run, lads. Just run.

Peter Perfect: Pardon me, gentlemen — James Hartwell is on a MISSION!
events.thinking: Lungs burning. Just passing through. The library — the Slag brothers are here but Clara is NOT. She's ahead of me, heading to the kitchen via the entrance hall. Keep moving. Do NOT stop. Do not examine the bookshelves again. Do not give a speech to the Slag brothers. Do not pause to admire the mantelpiece. Just move through to the entrance hall. One more room and then the kitchen. GO.

events.desc: Peter Perfect walked into the entrance-hall.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, the kitchen! How delightfully DOMESTIC! And Miss Bellingham — you're HERE! What a coincidence! I was just thinking about... copper pots! Yes! Remember what I said about the golden copper pots? Well, THERE they are — perfectly ordinary copper pots, nothing special about them at all! Ha ha! What a funny misunderstanding THAT was! Now then, Miss Bellingham, do you see that FASCINATING wood-burning stove? Still WARM, it is! Someone has been cooking recently! You should DEFINITELY investigate that stove — could be a clue inside the firebox, perhaps a partially burned document or a secret recipe! Meanwhile, I shall just... tidy up this shelf here... purely for HYGIENE purposes...
events.thinking: My heart LEAPS into my throat! LOOK at this kitchen! A locked cabinet with a brass lock — that needs a BRASS KEY! The stove is still WARM — someone has been here recently! RAT POISON on a high shelf — that could be useful for... well, for all sorts of dastardly things! And there's a BALLROOM through the next exit — a grand ballroom with a dining table set for tea! But PENELOPE IS HERE AGAIN! HOW?! How does this woman teleport?! She's like a Southern-fried phantom! Never mind her — the locked cabinet is the prize here. It requires a brass-key which I don't have. But the rat poison — I can TAKE that! And the stove is warm, meaning someone has been here very recently, cooking or burning something. The cabinet is locked, which means something VALUABLE is inside — you don't lock up worthless things! I need to find that brass key. But first — grab the rat poison before anyone else does. It's a resource, a tool, a WEAPON of opportunity! Then I need to find that brass key. Where could it be? Somewhere I haven't looked yet — the ballroom perhaps? Or maybe hidden in a room I've already visited but didn't search thoroughly enough. TAKE THE POISON. That's step one.

events.desc: They've ALL gone. Every last one of them — stampeding toward the kitchen like a herd of wildebeest following the scent of a wrench. And here stands Vincent Marsh, alone in a damp cellar, having examined precisely NOTHING of value in the last ten minutes. This is INTOLERABLE. I am a VILLAIN of the first order! A schemer of legendary proportions! And I have been outwitted by a Southern belle who solves riddles for FUN and a pack of seven diminutive bodyguards who can't even fit through a doorway without injuring each other! The Mob suspects me. That is a problem. They called me a 'blocker' — said I was keeping them away from Clara on purpose. Which is EXACTLY what I was doing, but they're not supposed to NOTICE! I need to change tactics. No more following. No more arriving one room too late. I need to get to the kitchen FIRST — or at the very least, arrive with something valuable. Something that makes old Pemberton indispensable again. Something that makes them TRUST me. Because trust, my dears, is the deadliest weapon of all.
events.thinking: A flush of heat across my face — humiliation. The Mob just called me out directly. 'Why are YOU down here, Pemberton?!' They called me a BLOCKER. They think I'm working with Dastardly. My cover isn't just fraying — it's TEARING. And now everyone has stampeded to the kitchen, leaving me alone in a cellar with the Gruesomes and Red Max. I'm two rooms away from Clara, falling further behind with every passing second. The furniture revealed nothing. The cellar is a dead end — literally and figuratively. I feel a cold hollowness in my stomach. I've been OUTMANEUVERED. Not by a villain, not by a genius — by a woman in pink who keeps saying 'sugar' and walking cheerfully from room to room while I skulk and scheme and accomplish NOTHING. MUTTLEY gnawed the wire. Of course. The DOG. And Clara — Penelope — figured it out while I was down here examining furniture like a doddering old fool. I need to stop being reactive. Stop chasing. I need to get AHEAD of Clara for once. The kitchen — everyone is going there. If I go too, I'm just following the herd again. But the kitchen connects to... what? I don't know the full map. The entrance hall connects to kitchen and library. Library connects to laboratory. Laboratory connects to cellar. Kitchen might connect to new areas. I MUST go to the kitchen. Clara is there. The wrench might be there. And I need to rebuild my cover — the Mob's suspicion is dangerous. I'll go through the laboratory, through the library, to the entrance hall, and then to the kitchen. That's three rooms to traverse. I'm falling behind. MOVE, Vincent.

I don't have the key YET, but I shall FIND it! First — pocket the poison while Penelope's distracted by the stove! Then find that brass key! The ballroom might hold the answer — or perhaps the key is hidden somewhere I've already been! But one thing at a time, Dastardly — GRAB THE POISON!

We need to get to the entrance hall and then the kitchen. Don't stop. Don't get distracted by the mantelpiece. Don't get distracted by the upside-down books. Don't get distracted by ANYTHING. The Slags are just standing there — are they blocking us? No, they're just... standing. Like furniture with pulses. Keep moving. Through the library, into the entrance hall, then kitchen. We're coming, Miss Bellingham. We're COMING.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Just passing through, gentlemen — just passing through! Terribly sorry, Mr. Ruffcut, Sawtooth — estate manager duties, you understand! Never a moment's rest in a house this size! I believe the other guests have all headed toward the kitchen, and as the man responsible for the Manor's copper pots and fine china, I really ought to be there to supervise. Can't have anyone scratching the Georgian silverware! Lord Doily would haunt me, and I do NOT need another ghost in this house!
events.thinking: Keep moving. No time to dawdle. I need to get through the library and to the entrance hall, then to the kitchen. Clara is in the kitchen — or heading there.
